perFinding.rationale: False positive for traversal at readSync: the reported flow starts with the explicit local --python option and follows fixed-bridge stdout into the receipt read. The trusted local interpreter executes fixed isolated Python code, returns only certified fixed-profile exchange names, and cannot obtain pins from receipt data. readSync consumes the previously opened descriptor, not a path string. stableBytes enforces canonical parent, ordinary single-link file, bounded size, no-follow read-only open, descriptor identity and before/after identity checks. Arbitrary operator-selected malicious executable is outside this trusted local invocation contract. Independent post-adoption review: the complete authority delta replaces only the fixed Hyperliquid v1 receipt digest 49027dc8f1c341f740e2cfa2f7229e9a07fbb640ff3db8ee494f978285b78e17 with 2304b4e1837925f546f7fdd3871a125a342a7f56ffeae4effbb66ac0219d7264; MappingProxyType key/profile/cardinality, imports, fixed-path construction, executable selection, no-shell spawn arguments and file-handle checks are unchanged. Actual installed receipt bytes in both scan and LF proof worktrees equal the new digest and exact independent62-requirement/968-input adoption approval. Pins still originate only from imported source authority; receipt JSON and CLI output cannot introduce a pin. This reaffirms the existing individually scoped local CLI finding, grants no provider acceptance and does not assert monitoring-container verification.

False positive for indirect command injection in this local CLI contract: the operator deliberately selects the absolute Python executable through the only accepted --python option. absolutePython, realpath, ordinary-file and canonical-parent checks precede spawnSync. The executable receives a fixed argument array with isolated -I, no-bytecode -B, literal bridge code and fixed repository root; shell is false, with timeout and output limits. No application request, receipt field or pin selects executable/code/import names. These checks do not certify an arbitrary malicious executable as safe; local executable selection remains operator authority. Pins still originate only from imported source authority; receipt JSON and CLI output cannot introduce a pin. This reaffirms the existing individually scoped local CLI finding, grants no provider acceptance and does not assert monitoring-container verification.

False positive for traversal at openSync: the reported stdout-derived exchange originates from fixed PROFILES via certification_result, which enforces a lowercase identifier grammar and equality to profile.id before looking up source-owned pins and validating receipt bytes/schema. Pins remain code-owned and have now been explicitly independently approved for the exact installed receipt.
